eligible.content: Yeah, I was thinking the same thing about the soy sauce. It's easy enough to add a little more later if someone wants it. But I'm still a little worried about the ginger—do you think it'll be too strong if I add it now?

The amount of ginger you add really depends on how much you like it! If you want a subtle hint of spice, start with a small amount—maybe a half teaspoon—and then taste it. If you want it to be a stronger flavor, you can add a little more.

Also, do you have a specific amount of rice you're using? Knowing that might help me tell you exactly how much to add for the best flavor!

sources.content: I think I'll add it at the end, just to be safe. But I'm still not sure about the rice—should I cook it first or mix it in with the other ingredients?

It really depends on what else you are putting in the rice! If you are just making simple fried rice, you might want to mix the sauce in towards the end of the cooking process. If you are mixing it with other ingredients like vegetables or proteins, adding it right before you're ready to eat might keep the texture and color looking its best.

Since you mentioned earlier, if you are using pre-cooked rice, you could either add the soy sauce in at the very end, just to "season" the final plate, or you could mix it in while it's still hot on the stove to help it absorb the flavor better. Which way sounds more like what you're trying to do?
I guess I'll mix it in while the rice is still hot, so the flavors can meld a bit. But I'll keep the soy sauce separate in case someone wants less. Does that make sense?
That makes perfect sense. Adding it when it's hot allows the flavors to blend in beautifully! Keep the extra soy sauce on the side if people want less—that's a great way to cater to different tastes!
